Seminar 01 Face-to-face seminar Complete entry

UplEEft: Empowering the Future, Human, and Technical Skills One Engineer

Program FlowSeminar Session 1
DateFebruary 20, 2026
Time1:00 PM – 4:00 PM
VenueAmphitheater, Albert Einstein Building, Batangas State University – The National Engineering University, Alangilan Campus

Group Facilitators

  • Group 1: composed of Group 1-1A, Group 1-2B, and Group 1-3C.
  • Group 2: composed of Group 2-4A, Group 2-1D, and Group 2-6C.
  • Group 3: composed of Group 3-7A, Group 3-8B, and Group 3-3D.
  • Group 4: composed of Group 4-3B and Group 4-6D.

Theme / Objective of the Seminar

The seminar “UplEEft: Empowering the Future, Human, and Technical Skills One Engineer” aimed to empower future engineers by developing both technical competence and human skills. It emphasized that engineering success requires not only technical expertise but also leadership, communication, adaptability, and ethical responsibility.

SCADA and Energy Efficiency Technical Discussion

Time1:05 PM – 1:40 PM
SpeakersEngr. Mark M. Labitoria – Project Manager, Automation / Technoplus Industrial Systems, Inc. (Main Guest Speaker); Engr. Raymond C. Fideli – BIZ Partner Manager, Distribution / South BIZ Area; Engr. Jayron Gallarda – Customer Service Manager, Distribution / South BIZ Area.

Key Points from the Speakers

  • Introduced SCADA and its function in real-time monitoring and remote control of electrical systems.
  • Explained the components of SCADA, including field devices, communication networks, and control centers.
  • Demonstrated how SCADA improves reliability and minimizes energy losses.
  • Highlighted SCADA applications in smart grids and efficient power distribution.
  • Connected theoretical concepts with actual industry practices.

Key Takeaways

The discussion emphasized that modern electrical systems increasingly rely on automation and intelligent monitoring technologies. SCADA enables engineers to maintain operational efficiency, quickly respond to system abnormalities, and optimize energy usage.

Reflection

This session broadened my understanding of how automation and monitoring systems are applied beyond classroom discussions. It made me realize that future engineers must continuously adapt to evolving technologies and understand how data-driven systems improve operational decision-making.

Application of Learning

As an Electrical Engineering student, I can apply this knowledge by strengthening my understanding of automation, power systems, and industrial controls. This also encourages me to explore SCADA applications and smart grid technologies that are becoming increasingly important in the energy sector.

From Student to Engineer: What They Don’t Teach You in School

Time1:50 PM – 2:25 PM
SpeakerEngr. Aljade B. Villafranca – Supervisor Engineer / Consolidated Explosive Group Corporation.

Key Points from the Speaker

  • Explained the difference between academic learning and industry expectations.
  • Emphasized that engineering solutions must work safely and efficiently in actual environments.
  • Discussed the importance of maintaining a safety-first mindset.
  • Highlighted leadership, communication, and emotional intelligence as essential skills.

Key Takeaways

Technical competence alone is not enough to succeed in engineering. Character, responsibility, teamwork, and safety awareness are equally important in becoming an effective and trusted professional.

Reflection

This discussion made me realize that academic excellence should be paired with professional discipline and accountability. Success in engineering depends not only on solving problems correctly but also on ensuring safety, managing teams effectively, and making sound decisions under pressure.

Application of Learning

As an Electrical Engineering student, I can begin preparing for professional practice by developing communication skills, strengthening leadership abilities, and practicing accountability in academic projects and group activities. Building these habits early will help bridge the gap between student life and industry expectations.

The Road to a Better You: Personal Development

Time2:35 PM – 3:10 PM
SpeakerRev. Ruwinner Aranas Delos Reyes – Pastor / Reverend / Bauan Bible Christian Church, Inc.

Key Points from the Speaker

  • Introduced the “Attitude Indicator” and how attitude influences success.
  • Discussed the Law of Influence and Law of the Bad Apple.
  • Presented seven attitudes for growth: gratefulness, integrity, hard work, resilience, servanthood, excellence, and interdependence.
  • Explained the Four-Directional Look framework.

Key Takeaways

Personal growth and professional success begin internally through mindset and values. Developing positive attitudes and maintaining integrity can significantly influence both individual performance and team success.

Reflection

This session reminded me that success is not measured only by achievements but also by how a person responds to challenges and interacts with others. The statement, “I got nothing to PROVE, but I got a lot of things to IMPROVE,” reinforced the importance of continuous self-development.

Application of Learning

As an Electrical Engineering student, I can apply these lessons by practicing resilience during academic challenges, maintaining a positive attitude during collaborative work, and continuously improving my personal habits to become both a competent and ethical engineer.

RA No. 9513 – Renewable Energy Act of 2008

Time3:20 PM – 3:50 PM
SpeakerEngr. Ian Medwin E. Dimaano, RME, SO2 – Technical Sales / Site Engineer / Surge Electrical Supplies and Contracting Corp.

Key Points from the Speaker

  • Explained the objectives and implementation of RA 9513.
  • Discussed renewable energy policies and governing bodies.
  • Introduced Renewable Portfolio Standards, Feed-In Tariff, Renewable Energy Market, and Renewable Energy Certificates.
  • Explained net metering and different solar system configurations.
  • Demonstrated practical monitoring applications used in actual projects.

Key Takeaways

The discussion emphasized that renewable energy development requires not only technical knowledge but also understanding government regulations, system integration, and sustainable energy practices. Net metering serves as an important mechanism for encouraging renewable energy adoption.

Reflection

This session increased my appreciation for renewable energy technologies and showed how policies directly support sustainable engineering practices. It demonstrated that engineers play a vital role in promoting cleaner and more efficient energy systems.

Application of Learning

As an Electrical Engineering student, I can apply this learning by expanding my knowledge of renewable energy systems, understanding local energy regulations, and considering sustainable design approaches in future engineering projects. This also motivates me to explore opportunities in solar and energy management industries.

Overall Key Takeaways

The “UplEEft: Empowering the Future, Human, and Technical Skills One Engineer” seminar emphasized that becoming a successful engineer requires more than technical knowledge alone. The sessions collectively demonstrated the importance of integrating technical expertise, innovation, professional ethics, communication, leadership, personal development, and adaptability in engineering practice.

Through the discussions on SCADA and energy efficiency, I gained awareness of the growing role of automation and intelligent systems in modern industries. The session on transitioning from student to engineer highlighted the realities of professional practice and reinforced the importance of accountability and safety.

The discussion on personal development emphasized that attitude, values, and interpersonal skills significantly influence long-term success, while the session on Renewable Energy Act of 2008 expanded my understanding of sustainable engineering and the practical implementation of renewable energy systems in the Philippines.

Overall, the seminar reinforced the idea that future engineers must become technically capable professionals who also demonstrate strong character, continuous learning, and social responsibility.

Overall Key Reflection

Attending this seminar allowed me to look beyond the technical aspects of engineering and understand the broader qualities required in the profession. I realized that engineering is not solely about designing systems or solving equations but also about making responsible decisions, working effectively with others, and continuously improving oneself.

One of the most meaningful realizations from the seminar was understanding that personal growth and professional competence must develop together. The speakers showed that engineering success is influenced by technical excellence, ethical standards, leadership abilities, and a positive mindset.

This seminar also encouraged me to reflect on my current preparation as an Electrical Engineering student and recognize areas where I can continue to grow—not only academically but also personally and professionally.

Overall Application of Learning

The learnings gained from this seminar can be applied throughout my academic journey and future engineering career by adopting a more holistic approach to development.

Academically, I can strengthen my technical foundation by exploring areas such as automation systems, energy efficiency, and renewable energy technologies. Professionally, I can practice leadership, communication, teamwork, and accountability during projects and collaborative activities.

Personally, I can apply the principles of resilience, integrity, and continuous self-improvement to become more adaptable and effective in handling challenges. Moving forward, I intend to develop both my technical competencies and human skills to become an engineer who not only delivers solutions but also creates meaningful and sustainable impact.

The colloquium presented and evaluated foundational and emerging engineering research across multiple disciplines. It served as a platform for examining technical proposals, design feasibility, and real-world engineering applications.

Underground Electrical Distribution Layout for Balayan, Batangas

Proponents / SpeakersGroup 1-1A

FrontiEErs 1.0: Foraging the Forefront of Engineering and Resilience

DateMarch 27, 2026
Time2:00 PM – 5:00 PM
Venue / PlatformZoom Cloud Link

Group Facilitators

  • Group 6: Group 6-2C and Group 6-4B.
  • Group 7: Group 7-3A, Group 7-5C, and Group 7-8D.
  • Group 8: Group 8-6A, Group 8-7B, and Group 8-8C.
  • Group 11: Group 11-7D, Group 11-8A, and Group 11-1B.
  • Group 12: Group 12-2A and Group 12-5D.

Theme / Objective

The seminar focused on advancing knowledge in maintenance and operations while strengthening mental resilience among students. It aimed to connect technical competence with emotional strength, promote industry readiness, and build a supportive engineering community.

Sessions / Presentations

Engineering Maintenance and Operation

Time2:10 PM – 3:05 PM
Proponents / SpeakersEngr. Allann R. Carolino
FocusMaintenance management

Engr. Allann R. Carolino – IIEE Batangas Chapter President

Key Highlights

  • Discussed the pillars of maintenance management and real applications in industrial plant operations.
  • Explained preventive and scheduled maintenance through daily, weekly, and monthly inspection routines.
  • Introduced predictive maintenance using IoT, vibration analysis or FFT, and infrared thermography.
  • Highlighted autonomous maintenance and the role of operators in basic equipment care.
  • Presented lean engineering tools such as Kaizen, Ishikawa Diagram, and Poka-Yoke for continuous improvement.

Key Takeaway

Maintenance engineering is proactive, not merely reactive troubleshooting. It protects reliability, safety, and efficiency by using discipline, monitoring, and data-driven analysis.

Reflection

This session helped me understand that engineering maintenance requires structured planning, continuous monitoring, and improvement rather than waiting for failure to occur.

Application of Learning

I can apply this by strengthening my understanding of maintenance principles, data-driven diagnostics, and preventive practices in electrical systems.

Mental Resilience

Time3:05 PM – 4:55 PM
Proponents / SpeakersPanel Speakers
FocusWell-being and resilience

Ms. Lara Dawn D. Calingasan – SSC Adviser, General Education Faculty
Mr. Iver Olin Napeñas-Sones, LPT – Lecturer I / Licensed Financial Advisor
Engr. Arren Jhunn B. Rivera – Petroleum Engineer, Safety Officer, SK Federation Secretary
Engr. James Torres – Registered Electrical Engineer, Resident Engineer, SM Engineering Design and Development

Key Highlights

  • Discussed mental health awareness, stress, burnout, and emotional fatigue in engineering education.
  • Differentiated stress and burnout and explained warning signs and coping approaches.
  • Presented coping strategies such as time management, mindfulness, prioritization, and balancing academic workload with personal life.
  • Encouraged seeking help, breaking stigma, and building support systems.
  • Shared real-life experiences about academic pressure, financial concerns, fear of failure, confidence, and self-compassion.

Key Takeaway

Mental resilience is as important as technical competence. Long-term success in engineering requires emotional balance, confidence, and healthy support systems.

Reflection

This session reminded me that many engineering students experience similar struggles, and asking for help is not a weakness but a necessary part of growth.

Application of Learning

I can apply these lessons by managing academic responsibilities more effectively, practicing self-care, and supporting a healthier academic environment.

FrontiEErs 1.0 emphasized that engineering success requires both technical mastery and personal resilience. The seminar linked maintenance management, predictive tools, system reliability, emotional resilience, and community support.

Overall Reflection

The seminar deepened my understanding of the challenges faced by engineering students and professionals. It showed that discipline, emotional strength, and resilience are essential in handling pressure and continuous demands.

Overall Application of Learning

I can apply the learning by improving my maintenance and diagnostics knowledge while also practicing stress management, self-awareness, and a balanced routine.

DateApril 1, 2026
Time8:00 AM – 11:00 AM

Theme / Objective

The seminar focused on exploration, innovation, and advancement in Electrical Engineering. It exposed participants to emerging technologies, modern industry practices, and engineering standards to prepare future engineers to be adaptable and technically competent.

Sessions / Presentations

Voltage Drop Calculation for Low, Medium, and High Voltage Settings

Time8:15 AM – 9:15 AM
Proponents / SpeakersEngr. Dennis A. Borlaza, PEE
FocusVoltage drop and standards

Engr. Dennis A. Borlaza, PEE – Professional Electrical Engineer, VP for Technical Affairs, IIEE Central Laguna Chapter, Power System Analysis and Facilities Management Specialist

Key Highlights

  • Explained the role of voltage drop analysis in electrical performance and safety.
  • Discussed factors affecting voltage drop such as conductor length, wire size, load current, conductor material, and temperature.
  • Demonstrated use of Ohm’s Law and engineering formulas for voltage losses.
  • Highlighted cable sizing, impedance, voltage regulation, and efficiency requirements.
  • Reinforced compliance with PEC, NEC, IEC, and IEEE standards.

Key Takeaway

Voltage drop calculation is a fundamental design practice that affects safety, efficiency, reliability, equipment performance, and standards compliance.

Reflection

The session made me realize that electrical design requires precision because small losses can significantly affect actual system operation.

Application of Learning

I can apply this by improving my calculation skills and becoming more attentive to technical details in future design work.

Proponents / SpeakersEngr. Dionisio G. Urbina Jr., REE
FocusBuilding electrical design

Engr. Dionisio G. Urbina Jr., REE – Principal Partner, Space Grupo Engineering Consultancy

Key Highlights

  • Explained the complexity of high-rise electrical systems and vertical development.
  • Discussed equipment sizing, load demand, temperature, voltage regulation, and code requirements.
  • Presented design principles such as flexibility, economy, safety, cost-effectiveness, and integrity.
  • Highlighted separation of power and data systems and the importance of emergency operations.
  • Demonstrated the role of Single Line Diagrams and dwelling unit calculations.

Key Takeaway

Reflection

This session showed me that design involves strategic planning and long-term decision-making beyond theoretical computations.

Application of Learning

I can apply this by improving my ability to interpret layouts, perform load analysis, and understand electrical design standards.

Synthesis of Learning

Connecting the EE 417 learning experience

After attending the EE 417 seminars, colloquia, and research conferences, I realized that electrical engineering is a diverse and continuously evolving field that combines technical expertise, innovation, sustainability, and professional responsibility. The different events expanded my understanding of how engineering concepts are applied in real-world situations to improve systems, solve practical problems, and contribute to society.

⚙️

Technical Competence

The seminars strengthened my knowledge of SCADA systems, voltage drop calculations, electrical design analysis, automation, power systems, renewable energy, power factor correction, energy management, and grid interconnection. I learned the importance of accurate calculations, system reliability, safety standards, and proper engineering practices in designing efficient and dependable electrical systems.

💡

Innovation and Creativity

The various research presentations demonstrated how innovation can transform engineering ideas into practical solutions. Projects involving solar-powered systems, automated machines, smart energy devices, irrigation systems, and automation platforms showed that creativity is essential in addressing real-world engineering challenges. These events inspired me to think critically and develop solutions that are both functional and beneficial to society.

🌱

Sustainability and Renewable Energy

Many of the seminars emphasized sustainability, renewable energy, and environmentally responsible engineering practices. Discussions on solar energy systems, net metering, wind turbines, energy-efficient infrastructures, and green architecture highlighted the role of electrical engineers in promoting sustainable development and reducing environmental impact.

🔎

Research and Problem-Solving

The colloquia enhanced my appreciation for research as an important part of engineering. I realized that research is not only about technical studies but also about identifying community problems, analyzing systems, testing solutions, and improving existing technologies. The events showed how engineering research can contribute to agriculture, public service, education, automation, and energy generation.

🤝

Professional and Personal Growth

Beyond technical knowledge, the seminars taught me the importance of professionalism, communication, adaptability, resilience, and responsibility in the engineering profession. The speakers emphasized that engineers must understand industry standards, government regulations, documentation, teamwork, and ethical responsibilities in order to become effective professionals.

Final Reflection

Overall Learning Reflection

Overall, the seminars and colloquia provided me with valuable knowledge and insights into the different fields of electrical engineering. The events covered a wide range of topics, including renewable energy, automation, electrical design, energy management, research innovation, and community-based engineering solutions. Through these discussions and presentations, I gained a deeper understanding of how engineering concepts are applied in real-world situations to solve practical problems and improve systems.

The seminars also helped me realize that being an effective electrical engineer requires more than technical knowledge alone. Engineers must also possess critical thinking, adaptability, communication skills, professionalism, and resilience in order to meet the challenges of the industry. The presentations from professionals, researchers, and fellow students inspired me to appreciate the importance of continuous learning, innovation, and research in the advancement of engineering practice.

Most importantly, these events motivated me to become more responsible, creative, and socially aware as a future engineer. They showed how electrical engineering can contribute to sustainability, renewable energy development, automation, public service, and community improvement. Overall, the experience strengthened my passion for the field and encouraged me to pursue engineering not only as a profession, but also as a way to contribute positively to society.

Technical awareness

I gained deeper knowledge of renewable energy, automation, electrical design, energy management, research innovation, and community-based engineering solutions.

Professional development

I realized that effective electrical engineers need critical thinking, adaptability, communication skills, professionalism, and resilience.

Innovation mindset

The seminars inspired me to appreciate continuous learning, innovation, and research in advancing engineering practice.

Social responsibility

I became more motivated to use electrical engineering to contribute to sustainability, public service, and community improvement.
